finalText:
**Merge** takes two branch histories and joins them with a new commit that has two parents. Your original commits stay exactly as they were, and you get a true record of when the branches diverged and came back together.

**Rebase** takes your commits and replays them one by one on top of a different starting point. It rewrites each commit with a new parent, so the result looks like you built your work straight on the latest code, in a straight line, with no branching at all.

Reach for **merge** when combining work into a shared branch like `main`, or any branch other people are also pulling from. It's safe because it never rewrites commits anyone else already has.

Reach for **rebase** to clean up your own local or feature branch before sharing it — folding in the latest `main`, tidying messy commits, keeping history readable. The one hard rule: never rebase commits you've already pushed and that someone else might have pulled. Doing that rewrites history out from under them and causes a real mess.
